history.heading: Comorian island
paragraphs: Mayotte is part of the Comoro archipelago in the Mozambique Channel. Its population descends from Bantu, Malagasy and Arab-Swahili settlers, and it was ruled by sultans. France acquired Mayotte in 1841, before the other Comoro islands.

In referendums in 1974 and 1976, Mayotte voted to remain French while the other islands became independent as the Comoros, which still claims Mayotte. A 2009 referendum made it an overseas department of France in 2011.

history.heading: Recent crises
paragraphs: Mayotte has faced water shortages, unrest and tensions over irregular migration from the Comoros and Africa. In December 2024 Cyclone Chido devastated the island, destroying many homes and informal settlements.

culture.heading: Mahoran culture
paragraphs: French is official, but most people speak Shimaore, a Swahili-related language, or Kibushi, related to Malagasy. Almost all are Sunni Muslim. Women often wear the salouva wrap and a face mask of sandalwood paste (msindzano). Mayotte's lagoon is one of the largest in the world.

politics.heading: French department
paragraphs: Mayotte is an overseas department and region of France and an outermost region of the EU. It elects representatives to the French parliament. The French government has passed special measures on migration and reconstruction.

economy.heading: Poorest French department
paragraphs: Mayotte is by far the poorest department of France, with a large share of the population living below the poverty line, many in informal housing. The public sector is the main employer, and the economy depends on French transfers, with small-scale farming, fishing and ylang-ylang. The currency is the euro.
